latestRelease.title: v1.40.1
latestRelease.notes:
## This is a patch release.

### What's Changed

- Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following `AUTH`, `SELECT`, `HELLO`, `CLIENT`, or `RESET` now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state ([#8016](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8016)).
- Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation ([#8011](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8011), [#8014](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8014)).

Full Changelog: [v1.40.0...v1.40.1](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.40.0...v1.40.1)
highlights: Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following AUTH, SELECT, HELLO, CLIENT, or RESET now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state (#8016).
Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation (#8011, #8014).

"tiered_prefix": "/tmp/tiered/pause_v2_backing", "tiered_offload_threshold": "1.0", "tiered_experimental_cooling": "false", "maxmemory": "2G", } ) async def test_client_pause_v2_inflight_async_write_gap(df_server: DflyInstance): """Regression: an in-flight async command on the V2 loop must keep CLIENT PAUSE waiting. A tiered APPEND parks the shard fiber on a disk read, so the command stays in-flight while returning a tiny reply. CLIENT PAUSE WRITE must not return until it completes. Tuning parameter: VALUE_BYTES (make the disk read long enough to stay in-flight). """ # Skip for V1 even if workflow injected --df enable_resp_io_loop_v2=false, which overrides the @dfly_args default above. if not is_resp_io_loop_v2(df_server): pytest.skip("targets the V2 io loop deferred-checkpoint path") VALUE_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024 # 256MB populator = df_server.client() writer = df_server.client() pauser = df_server.client() await populator.execute_command("DEBUG", "POPULATE", 1, "huge", VALUE_BYTES, "RAND") keys = await populator.keys("huge*") assert len(keys) == 1 big_key = keys[0] # Wait until the value is offloaded to disk (else APPEND reads from memory instantly). async with async_timeout.timeout(60): while int((await populator.info("TIERED")).get("tiered_entries", 0)) < 1: await asyncio.sleep(0.2) # Async write that must fetch the whole value from disk. Race them: a correct server writes # the APPEND reply before releasing the pause checkpoint, so APPEND wins. If PAUSE wins, the # write slipped past CLIENT PAUSE - the bug. signals.title: ZMPOP RESP2 reply is incompatibile with Redis
signals.text:
# `ZMPOP` returns the wrong RESP2 null type when no member can be popped **NOTE**: I found this issue when adding `dragonfly` to PhpRedis' CI (https://github.com/phpredis/phpredis/pull/2907). This surfaced about half a dozen reply shape incompatibilities with Redis. If perfect compatibility isn't a goal of dragonfly just let me know and I can instead update our tests **Describe the bug** When no member can be popped, Dragonfly returns a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1
`) instead of the null array (`*-1
`) returned by Redis. RESP2 null bulk strings and null arrays are distinct wire types even though some clients map both to the same language-level value. PhpRedis parses `ZMPOP` with its multi-bulk response parser. Dragonfly's null bulk string does not match the expected aggregate response type, so PhpRedis rejects the response and returns `false` instead of the expected empty result or `null`. **To Reproduce** 1. Connect using RESP2 to databases where `zs` does not exist or is empty. 2. Run `ZMPOP 1 zs MIN` against Redis and Dragonfly. 3. Compare the wire responses. In the example below, port 6379 is Redis and port 9999 is Dragonfly. ```console $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 6379 *-1 $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 $-1 ``` **Expected behavior** Like Redis, Dragonfly should return a RESP2 null array: ```text *-1
 ``` `ZMPOP` otherwise returns an aggregate containing the selected key and popped members, so its nil result should retain the aggregate response type. **Screenshots** Not applicable; the raw protocol responses are included above. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Not recorded - Kernel: Not recorded - Containerized?: Not recorded - Dragonfly Version: `df-v1.39.0` Redis control version: `8.9.241` Protocol: RESP2 **Reproducible Code Snippet** ```sh printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 ``` **Additional context** With `Redis::OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL` enabled, PhpRedis recognizes a null array as an empty `ZMPOP` result and returns it to PHP as `null`. This mismatch causes `Redis_Test::testZmpop` to fail: ```text Assertion failed: testZmpop - (false) !== (null) ``` Dragonfly's `ZMPopGeneric` empty-result path calls `SendNull()`: - [ZMPOP implementation](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/server/zset_family.cc) - [RESP reply builder](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/facade/reply_builder.cc) For RESP2, `SendNull()` emits `$-1
`. The reply builder has a distinct `SendNullArray()` method which emits `*-1
`. Dragonfly also returns `$-1
` for an empty or timed-out `BZMPOP`. The current PhpRedis `testBZmpop` only asserts the default `false` result, so it does not expose the type mismatch through `OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL`.
signals.author: michael-grunder

signals.title: fix(server): emit expired keyspace events when the new expiration is already in the past
signals.text: Deleting a key because its newly-set expiration is already in the past emitted no `__keyevent@<db>__:expired` notification, so subscribers waited forever (found via the upstream Valkey pubsub TCL suite: "expired event (Expiration time is already expired)" hangs). There are exactly two silent-delete paths: `SET` with a past `EXAT/PXAT` (incl. memcached SET/ADD/REPLACE) and `DbSlice::UpdateExpire` (EXPIRE family, GETEX, GAT). Both now emit the event after journaling (mutation -> journal -> publish). Fixing this surfaced several adjacent bugs in the same paths and in the config plumbing that gates the events - all fixed here to keep the fix correct. Changes: **Core fix** - New `DbSlice::SendExpiredKeyEvent()`, called by all past-expiry delete paths after their journal record; `UpdateExpire` delete branch also counts `expired_keys` stats. **Correctness bugs exposed in the same paths** - `SET` with a past expiry short-circuited parsing: NX/XX/GET were ignored (`SET k v NX PXAT <past>` deleted the key and replied OK), trailing garbage was accepted, `PXAT == now` made the key persistent, and mc REPLACE-on-missing reported STORED. The early-return is gone; conditions go through the regular SetCmd machinery; the delete reuses `UpdateExpire`. - `SET` is NO_AUTOJOURNAL and the past-expiry delete was not journaled -> replicas kept the key forever. It now journals `DEL` (same for GETEX, which journaled a past `PEXPIREAT`). - Pre-existing: memcached `GAT 0` persists the key on master but journaled `PEXPIREAT key 0`, so replicas deleted it. It now journals `PERSIST`. **Config plumbing (gates the events, `notify_keyspace_events`)** - `ConfigRegistry::Set` rolls back the flag value when the validation callback rejects it; previously the rejected value stayed visible via CONFIG GET and raw flag reads. - New DbSlices inherit a validated process-global default instead of re-reading the raw flag, closing a race where a namespace created during CONFIG SET could read an unvalidated value and kill the process (the ctor also demanded exact "Ex" while the validator accepts "EX"). - `CONFIG SET notify_keyspace_events` now updates every namespace, not only the default one (new `Namespaces::ForEachDbSliceOnShard`). - Startup validation moved to dfly_main before the pidfile/listeners exist; an invalid flag previously exited mid-init with code 0, leaving a stale pidfile and unix socket. **TLS (follow-ups from the registry rollback making callback side effects observable)** - The `tls` callback builds the SSL_CTX once before touching listeners (new infallible `Listener::ApplyTlsCtx`), so a bad cert can no longer leave listeners split between old and new TLS state. - TLS memory accounting is now a global atomic: contexts are allocated on one thread and freed on another, so the summed per-thread counters wrapped `tls_bytes` to ~UINT64_MAX after reload. Tests: - Unit: expired events for EXPIRE/SET/GETEX/GAT/mc SET/REPLACE; SET past-expiry condition semantics; config rollback, all-namespaces propagation, hermetic restores of prior config. - Pytest: `GAT 0` persist replication, past-expiry SET DEL replication, `tls_bytes` regression with main+admin listeners; TLS suite passes end-to-end.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: feat(geo): add GEOSEARCHSTORE command
signals.text: <!-- **Commits Must Be Signed and Your PR title must conform to the conventional commit spec** * See: https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md * Please follow the section on `pre-commit hooks`, a linter will validate before you push Example PR Title: <type>(<scope>)!: <description> * `type` = bug, chore, feat, fix, docs, build, style, refactor, perf, test * `!` = OPTIONAL: signals a breaking change * `scope` = Optional when `type` is "chore" or "docs" * `description` = short description of the change Examples: * chore(examples): Clarify `docker` usage #120 * docs(readme): Fix Example Links #121 * feat(ingest)!: Add new ingest #122 * fix(ingest): Refactor for loop to list comprehension #123 --> Adds GEOSEARCHSTORE (dest + src keys, same search options as GEOSEARCH, optional STOREDIST). Most of the work was already in GeoSearchStoreGeneric() via GEORADIUS ... STORE — this wires up the dedicated command and parser. Closes #3883. Also fixed a couple of Redis mismatches in the shared store/search path: - STORE when the source key is missing now returns 0 and clears the dest key (was an empty array) - COUNT without ASC/DESC now defaults to ASC, same as Redis Tests in geo_family_test.cc. Ran geo_family_test locally + manual redis-cli checks.

signals.title: fix(server): lower table growth margin default
signals.text: ## Summary - Lower the default `table_growth_margin` from `0.4` to `0.15`. - Reduce the conservative free-capacity estimate before allowing table growth. ## Test plan - `git diff --check` passed. - `ninja -C build-dbg dragonfly` reached and compiled `src/server/db_slice.cc`; the full build was blocked by the host filesystem running out of space.
signals.author: romange

signals.title: fix(tiering): tight small bin fragmentation cutoff
signals.text: For small bins, the smallest possible utilization for flushing a page is ~49% (because value + constant size header). We don't want this page to be considered for defragmentation (as it will livelock) so we pick a cutoff that is slightly lower (see the math on the PR). Also StashInfo.bytes `undercounted` because it never `included` the bytes wasted by each entry's header. Fix it by including the header entry overhead per value. Addresses properly both #8029 and #8024 and #8012
signals.author: kostasrim

signals.title: fix: SET with a past expiration honors NX/XX/GET and journals the delete
signals.text: `SET k v [NX|XX|GET] EXAT/PXAT <past>` short-circuited parsing and unconditionally deleted the key replying OK: NX/XX/GET were ignored, trailing options were accepted unparsed, an expiration equal to now made the key persistent, and the delete was not journaled at all (SET is NO_AUTOJOURNAL), permanently desyncing replicas. Memcached SET/ADD/REPLACE with a past absolute exptime shared all of it. Changes: - The parser only marks `SetParams::expire_in_past` (now also for `== now`) and keeps parsing; `SetCmd::Set` evaluates NX/XX/GET through the regular condition machinery before applying delete-instead-of-store, matching upstream semantics. - The delete reuses `UpdateExpire` (same stats), journals an explicit `DEL`, and emits the expired keyspace event after the journal record.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: fix: test_cron_snapshot_failed_saving
signals.text: Summary: Re-enables the cron snapshot failure integration test using an isolated output directory. Changes: - Creates deterministic DFS temporary-path sentinels to force local snapshot writes to fail. - Starts a one-shard Dragonfly instance and enables the cron schedule only after capturing metric baselines. - Waits for both attempted-backup and failed-backup metrics, then verifies cleanup of temporary paths. - Uses a guarded explicit SHUTDOWN NOSAVE flow to prevent teardown from creating an unwanted snapshot. Technical Notes: The test avoids permission-based failures, making it safe when the test process runs as root and preventing shared temporary-directory contamination.
signals.author: BorysTheDev

signals.title: fix(tests): Sample lag continuously in test_replication_info
signals.text: test_replication_info relied on a fixed number of sampling attempts to catch lag exceeding 30 during a write burst, which could miss the actual peak and fail. Instead, sample lag continuously for the duration of the fill and check the max lag observed. target_ops is also increased to prolong the burst. assert_lag_condition now polls until the condition is met or a timeout is reached, rather than a fixed number of attempts. signals.title: fix(facade): Handle RESP3 null array response
signals.text: RESP3 expects "_\r\n" for a null array, but SendNullArray() always sent RESP2's "*-1\r\n" regardless of protocol. This fixed null replies under RESP3 for XREAD, XREADGROUP, BLPOP, BRPOP, BZPOPMIN, and BZPOPMAX. signals.title: test: un-skip graceful shutdown test by asserting the guaranteed durability contract
signals.text: `test_gracefull_shutdown` (skipped since #1530) asserted strict equality between the last acknowledged INCR value and the snapshot content - a reply-before-close guarantee the server does not provide: shutdown drains in-flight commands for at most 10ms (best effort) and, at the TCP level, closing with unread request bytes triggers RST, so reply delivery cannot be guaranteed to a busy client at all. The invariant that *does* hold (snapshot is saved strictly after all connection fibers exit) is one-directional: every acknowledged write is in the snapshot, and at most one unacknowledged in-flight command per connection may exceed it. The test now asserts exactly that contract, deterministically. Changes: - Un-skip and rename to `TestGracefulShutdown::test_shutdown_snapshot_contains_acknowledged_writes` - Assert `acknowledged <= restored <= acknowledged + 1` per key, plus an explicit missing-key check - Dedicated control connection for SHUTDOWN; one pinned connection per worker with client retries disabled (the client library retries by default, and a silent re-send after a lost reply would corrupt acknowledgment accounting) - All SETs acknowledged before the increment loops start, so every key must exist after restart - `df_server.wait()` before restarting (snapshot fully written, no port race) and `wait_available_async()` after (avoid the loading phase) - Dynamic port instead of hardcoded 1111 Addresses the `test_gracefull_shutdown` item in #8028.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: fix(server): probe heterogeneous blocking waiters instead of aborting…
signals.text: ## Summary `BlockingController` keeps one FIFO queue per `(db, key)` shared by *all* blocking commands watching that key. `NotifyWatchQueue()` only checked the front waiter: when its checker returned `kKeyNotFound` (e.g. `BLPOP`/`BZPOP*`/`BLMPOP` on a missing key), the scan aborted entirely and the one-shot wake event was cleared, so any *later* waiter in the same queue, from a different command family, was never checked at all. Concretely: a client blocked on `XREADGROUP` queued behind an earlier `BLPOP` waiter on the same key would never receive its `NOGROUP` error when the key was deleted. It stayed blocked indefinitely, only released later by an unrelated mutation of the key. ## Fix `NotifyWatchQueue` no longer aborts the whole scan on `kKeyNotFound`. It now tracks the checker (command family) that reported the key missing, and only fast-skips *later* waiters sharing that exact checker, this preserves the O (1)-per-item short-circuit from #7225 for the common homogeneous case (many `BLPOP` waiters on one absent key). Waiters from a different command family (e.g. `XREADGROUP` sharing a queue with `BLPOP`) are still probed individually, so they get the correct, immediate result instead of being hidden behind an unrelated waiter's outcome. ## Test plan - [x] New regression test `BlockingControllerTest.NotifyWatchQueueHeterogeneousCheckers`- two waiters with different checker types on one key's queue; the first reports `kKeyNotFound`, and the test asserts the second is still probed. - [x] Existing `BlockingControllerTest.NotifyWatchQueueFastPathOnAbsentKey` (the #7225 perf regression test) still passes unmodified, same-checker-type fast path is preserved. - [x] `blocking_controller_test`, `stream_family_test`, `list_family_test`, `zset_family_test` all passes. - [x] `pre-commit` (clang-format et al.) clean. Fixes #8067
signals.author: Shikha-code36

signal.title: fix(server): lower table growth margin default
signal.text: ## Summary - Lower the default `table_growth_margin` from `0.4` to `0.15`. - Reduce the conservative free-capacity estimate before allowing table growth. ## Test plan - `git diff --check` passed. - `ninja -C build-dbg dragonfly` reached and compiled `src/server/db_slice.cc`; the full build was blocked by the host filesystem running out of space.
